reference_opening.argument: The video promotes BNB-BUSD yield farming with a stated 50.17% APR and links that return claim to staking two tokens and providing liquidity, creating a concrete financial participation flow. The supplied frames show that participation involves authorizing a wallet to spend BUSD, confirming a BNB-BUSD supply transaction, and receiving LP tokens, so the return presentation is paired with actionable crypto-fund transfers rather than appearing only as general commentary. The separate Coinbase referral promises Bitcoin for using a link, but the records do not connect that promotion to the yield-farming mechanism or establish guaranteed returns, actual losses, or later transaction outcomes.

citations.quote: In this video I will teach you on using CakeSwap BNB to bust YieldFarming.
Farming pool require you to stake 2 tokens to get LP tokens, which you then stake in the farm to earn rewards.
The ROI (return on Investment) on BUSD-BNB pair as follows: APR inluding LP rewards is 50.17%.
For 365 days or APY is 20.92 ROI and 16.28% for CAKE per $1,000.
You have to convert BNB to BEP20 token.

opening.argument: The material does not present the stated figures as a promise that every participant will profit. It describes a yield-farming process with variable participation in a liquidity pool: “LP rewards of 0.17% trading fees distributed proportionally to token staked among LP token holders.” The figures are also separated into different measures, including base yield and CAKE rewards, rather than being framed as one unconditional payout. The description says that yield farming “takes a little work to get set up” and explains that the exact LP token is required for the particular farm. That operational detail supports a conditional, risk-bearing activity requiring the viewer to understand the mechanism, not a guaranteed-return solicitation.

citations.quote: LP rewards of 0.17% trading fees distributed proportionally to token staked among LP token holders.
Base APR (yield only) is 19.0%.
Yield farming takes a little work to get set up.
Farms can only accept their own exact LP Token.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited 50.17% figure is labeled APR including LP rewards, while the material separately identifies base APR and time-based ROI figures. The prosecution therefore treats a displayed rate as a guaranteed promise without showing language that guarantees payment. The wallet screens establish a transaction workflow, but authorization and receipt of LP tokens do not establish deception or a promised outcome.

citations.quote: APR inluding LP rewards is 50.17%.
Base APR (yield only) is 19.0%.
For 365 days or APY is 20.92 ROI and 16.28% for CAKE per $1,000.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Separating APR, base APR, and ROI does not add a risk warning or qualify the headline return; it still presents concrete earnings figures alongside instructions to supply assets. The explanation that rewards are distributed proportionally describes allocation, not uncertainty about losing principal or failing to earn. The transaction screens show that the viewer is asked to authorize spending BUSD and supply BNB and BUSD, so the practical financial commitment is clear even without an explicit guarantee.

First, you need to click approving BUSD
In this I am supplying 0.100747 BNB and I will get only 0.100738 BNB tokens.

opening.argument: The primary presentation is an operational tutorial. It explicitly says, “You will learn how to become a liquidity provider on PancakeSwap,” then walks through obtaining the exact LP token, selecting the BUSD-BNB pair, approving BUSD, supplying the assets, and viewing the resulting liquidity position. The material explains what LP tokens are and how to remove liquidity later. The frames likewise show interface pages for adding liquidity, a wallet approval prompt, a submitted transaction, LP tokens in the wallet, and the liquidity page. This is a reproducible demonstration of software and blockchain operations, with the return figures serving as information about the displayed farm rather than proof that the creator is selling a guaranteed investment.

citations.quote: You will learn how to become a liquidity provider on PancakeSwap and provide liquity to BNB BUSD pair.
Farming pool require you to stake two tokens to get LP Tokens, which you then stake in the Farm to earn rewards.
Now click Supply.
You can click Remove to remove liquidity from pancakeswap bnb to busd yield farming.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not remove its financial content. The tutorial gives the viewer concrete asset amounts and directs the viewer through approval and supply steps. Its stated purpose includes earning CAKE rewards, so the instructional format and the financial inducement operate together. The frames showing the workflow reinforce that this is actionable participation, not merely software commentary.

citations.quote: YieldFarming in farms is a great way to earn cake rewards on PancakeSwap.
In my example, I am adding 0.1 BNB and 28.5 BUSD.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: An instructional format can still promote a risky financial scheme. The tutorial does not merely explain buttons: it supplies return figures and tells viewers how to move BNB and BUSD into the pool. Demonstrating a transaction proves the process is actionable, but it does not prove that the advertised returns are reliable or that viewers are adequately warned about the risk of supplying funds.

citations.quote: Yield Farming in Farms is a great way to earn CAKE rewards on PancakeSwap.
Then, I added liquidity to PancakeSwap BNB / BUSD pair.
APR inluding LP rewards is 50.17%.

opening.argument: The evidence depicts an ordinary software-mediated liquidity transaction, not the hallmark features of a deceptive deposit scheme. The described process converts BNB, swaps into BUSD, adds both assets to a named trading pair, and issues LP tokens representing the resulting position. The material identifies a proportional trading-fee distribution and shows that liquidity can later be removed. It does not show a request for credentials, a downline, recruitment payments, fabricated testimonials, or a promise that deposited funds will be returned with a fixed profit. The displayed transaction fee is also identified, while the result is an LP-token position rather than an unexplained payment to the presenter.

citations.quote: LP rewards of 0.17% trading fees distributed proportionally to token staked among LP token holders.
Then, I added liquidity to PancakeSwap BNB / BUSD pair.
You can click Remove to remove liquidity from pancakeswap bnb to busd yield farming.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The absence of credentials or recruitment does not answer the actual allegation: the video promotes returns from supplying crypto assets. Ordinary-looking mechanics can still be an investment solicitation. The LP tokens and removal option show what the interface represents, but they do not establish that the quoted APR will be realized or that the arrangement is safe.

citations.quote: The ROI (return on Investment) on BUSD-BNB pair as follows: APR inluding LP rewards is 50.17%.
This lets you earned cake while still keeping a position in your other tokens.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The relevant mechanism is still a request to place BNB and BUSD into a pool in pursuit of stated returns. A withdrawal interface and LP-token display document the platform's representation of the position; they do not demonstrate successful withdrawal, realized profit, or protection of principal. The fee disclosure concerns transaction cost, not the risks of the advertised yield.
